title: Linearity of the profile decomposition gates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinate indices, and let $a:\mathbb{N}\to\{−1,1\}$ be a sign sequence. For each coordinate $i$, form a main gate that is constantly $1$ if $a(i+1)=a(i)$, and otherwise tests whether the number of coordinates in $S$ taking value $1$ is at least $i+1$, with output $1$ when $a(i+1)=1$ and output $-1$ otherwise. Pair it with a correction gate that is constantly $-1$ if $a(i+1)=a(i)$ and otherwise constantly $a(i+1)$. Every gate in this resulting family of $2n$ gates is a linear threshold function.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite subset of the $n$ coordinate indices
